title: QUIZ - 96
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Evaluating Truth Values of Multiple Statements
questions.learningObjective: Independently evaluate the truth values of two separate statements
questions.question: Consider these two statements: (1) "3 plus 4 equals 7." and (2) "A hexagon has five sides.". Which best describes their truth values?

options.label: A
options.text: Statement (1) is true and statement (2) is false.

options.label: B
options.text: Statement (1) is false and statement (2) is true.

questions.explanation: Statement (1) is true, and statement (2) is false.
questions.hint: Evaluate each statement independently before comparing their truth values.

questions.concept: Determining Truth Values
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a given declarative statement is true or false
questions.question: What is the truth value of the statement: "9 is a perfect square."?
questions.explanation: The statement "9 is a perfect square." is true because it accurately describes a verifiable fact.
questions.hint: A statement's truth value is determined by checking whether it accurately describes reality.

questions.concept: Defining Logical Statements
questions.learningObjective: Recall the formal definition of a logical statement or proposition
questions.question: How is a proposition defined in the study of logic?

options.label: A
options.text: Any sentence, regardless of whether it can be judged true or false.

options.label: B
options.text: A question that requests information from the listener.

options.label: C
options.text: A declarative sentence that is either true or false, but not both.

options.label: D
options.text: A command that instructs someone to perform an action.

questions.explanation: In logic, a statement (or proposition) must be a declarative sentence with a definite truth value: exactly one of true or false, never both, never neither.
questions.hint: A statement must be capable of being judged true or false — questions and commands cannot be statements.
